---
title: "Roadmap"
date-modified: 2026-09-30
---

Four milestones, in dependency order. Each has an **umbrella tracking issue** in this
repo where progress is checked off; implementation issues are filed in the repo where
the work happens ([where to file issues](index.qmd#where-to-file-issues)) and linked
from the umbrella's checklist. This page is the narrative; the issues are the ledger.
When they disagree, fix whichever is wrong.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  M0["M0 · Operational readiness<br/>hygiene, CI, health checks"] --> M1["M1 · Production cutover<br/>flipped 2026-09-28"]
  M1 --> M2["M2 · Full disconnect<br/>retire master, staging,<br/>build system, stats"]
  M1 --> M3["M3 · Search + redesigns<br/>prove the PR process"]
```

## M0 — Operational readiness ([#1](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/1))

The floor the rest stands on: every repo public, consistently named, licensed,
contributable, tested, and watched. Mostly done 2026-08-21.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Four public repos under the `bioc-*` convention, each with LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT (the original four: bioc-website, bioc-edge, bioc-registry, bioc-infrastructure; bioc-build and bioc-manifest, added since, have all three as of 2026-09-30)
- [x] Histories verified free of credentials and undisclosed findings
- [x] CI with badges on every repo
- [x] Daily black-box health checks with status badges — serving ([health](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge/actions/workflows/health.yml)) and data plane ([freshness](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-registry/actions/workflows/freshness.yml))
- [ ] CD: the workers deploy from CI on `main`, not from laptops
- [x] This roadmap, with umbrella issues

**Dependencies:** none.

## M1 — Production cutover ([#2](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/2))

**Done: `bioconductor.org` is served by the new edge since 2026-09-28** (nameservers to
Cloudflare at 17:30 UTC, the site at about 20:09 UTC; [runbook and log](dns-cutover.qmd)).
What remains is closing out the flip: the week of monitoring ends 2026-10-05, and Route53
stays the rollback target, with a record freeze, until 2026-10-12. How the system works now
is on [How bioconductor.org works](how-it-works.qmd); who runs it and the rollback steps are
on [Operations](operations.qmd).

Several pre-flip gates were overtaken by the flip itself. They are restated below as what
the running system has to show, with what replaced each.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] DNS flipped (2026-09-28)
- [x] `BiocManager::install()` acceptance passes for release + devel against `bioconductor.org` (3.23 and 3.24, after the flip)
- [x] Behaviour under real load measured, in place of a synthetic load test: 530,455 requests in two hours on 2026-09-29, 63% served from the edge cache, no Worker exceptions (Logpush, 16:00-18:00 UTC)
- [x] Rollback written up: [Operations, roll back DNS](operations.qmd#rollback-dns) and the [DNS runbook](dns-cutover.qmd). Not rehearsed; the lever stays in place until 2026-10-12
- [ ] Parity with master, in place of the pre-flip crawl diff: a probe of 13,271 paths from production logs (2026-09-29) found the differences in bioc-edge [#43](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge/issues/43)-[#48](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge/issues/48), all open; `parity.yml` compares production with master daily
- [ ] A week of monitoring with no unexplained regressions (ends 2026-10-05). Regressions found and fixed so far are in [improvements](improvements.qmd)
- [ ] Logging continuity: gap alerting is running (`bioc-logpush-check`, [CI & scheduled jobs](ci.qmd)); both log eras queryable as one is not
- [ ] Upstream security findings resolved with the Bioconductor core team
- [ ] Core team sign-off on the cutover as it stands (no sign-off is recorded here)

Checkboxes here mirror [#2](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/2).

**Tasks**

- [x] Cutover runbook page (DNS, verification, rollback): [DNS runbook](dns-cutover.qmd)
- [x] Flip
- [ ] Fix bioc-edge #43-#48, then close M1
- [ ] Decide `www.` / `secure.` and satellite hostnames ([DNS runbook, open questions](dns-cutover.qmd#open-questions-for-the-core-team))
- [ ] Walk the security findings with the core team
- [ ] After 2026-10-12: end the record freeze and retire the Route53 zone, or decide to keep it

**Dependencies:** M0 — the daily checks are what watches the flip.

## M2 — Full disconnect from legacy infrastructure ([#3](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/3))

The new stack serves production but still depends on master: packages arrive by the hourly
sync from master's docroot, and `/packages/stats/` is passed through to master. M2 ends
the dependency: master, staging, the legacy build system, and the legacy stats pipeline
all retire, and roughly $5,000/month of AWS with them. Parity with master
(bioc-edge [#43](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge/issues/43)-[#48](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge/issues/48))
has to be clean before master goes.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Prose content changes by PR in bioc-website. Pages are being ported one at a time; until the core team decides who owns the content, [Bioconductor/bioconductor.org](https://github.com/Bioconductor/bioconductor.org) stays the source ([Astro site build](astro-site-build.qmd))
- [ ] Hourly rsync from the legacy docroot retired — new content arrives only via CI builds and registry propagation
- [ ] Annotation, experiment, and workflow packages have a build home (r-universe covers software only — the open workstream)
- [ ] Download stats derive from the new edge logs, historical eras joined
- [x] Search off legacy Solr: production search is Pagefind over the Astro build (checked 2026-09-30); the design ADR stays in M3
- [ ] master + staging snapshotted, powered off, DNS retired
- [ ] The legacy AWS bill ends

**Tasks**

- [ ] Port prose pages into bioc-website one at a time; decide content ownership with the core team
- [ ] Sync-source retirement plan (what still changes upstream post-cutover, and who publishes it instead)
- [ ] Software repositories served from bioc-registry instead of the BBS mirror: [plan](registry-switch.qmd), [#35](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/35)
- [ ] Build-home decision for annotation/experiment/workflow, with the core team and the r-universe track
- [ ] Stats surface + continuity decision; then drop the `/packages/stats/` passthrough to master
- [ ] Final snapshots per the [decommission plan](decommission-plan.qmd); decommission
- [ ] Record the end state in the migration record

**Dependencies:** M1, done except for the parity fixes, which M2 needs too.

## M3 — Search and page redesigns, through the public PR process ([#4](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/4))

Two goals in one: a real search story, and visible redesign work used deliberately to
prove the contribution loop — PR → preview URL → review → merge → route flip.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Search design recorded as an ADR (scope, index strategy, fate of the Solr routes)
- [ ] Search live on the production Astro-built routes
- [ ] Two or more page redesigns shipped end-to-end through the public PR flow
- [ ] Contributor docs good enough that an outside contributor gets a preview URL unaided

**Tasks**

- [ ] Revisit the July 2026 findability and UX/IA audits (`audit/review/`); pick candidates
- [ ] Search ADR — Pagefind already indexes the Astro build; measure it at full-site scale first
- [ ] Prototype search over the full ported surface
- [ ] Ship redesign PRs #1 and #2; fold the friction into CONTRIBUTING
- [ ] Invite at least one outside contributor through the flow

**Dependencies:** none left; M1 put the Astro build in production.
